data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2021 the Syndicate's gross claims outstanding were GBP 839.0m. Analysis of the gross claims development table for underwriting years up to 2019 shows no material net prior-year movement at the gross level (net change ~GBP 0.0m), i.e., prior-year reserves were broadly stable. The syndicate experienced significant natural catastrophe activity (Storm Uri, Hurricane Ida, Texas freeze and active Atlantic seasons) and material Covid-19 related event cancellation losses which affected underwriting years around 2019-2020. During 2021 the Syndicate also completed a Reinsurance-to-Close of 2017 & prior transferring liabilities of GBP 279.4m to another syndicate, which materially reduced earlier year liabilities on this syndicate's balance sheet. Overall the prior-year reserve position is reported as broadly unchanged on a gross basis, with catastrophe and pandemic-related exposures being the key causal factors.

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding (839.0) taken from the statement of financial position / claims note at 31 Dec 2020. Prior-year development derived from the gross claims development table (current estimates vs previous diagonal) which indicates no material net movement for underwriting years up to 2019 (total ~GBP 0.0m). There is an RITC (2017 & prior) transaction during 2021 transferring GBP 279.4m of liabilities out of the syndicate which materially alters comparative balances; this has been recorded where explicitly stated. The report includes explicit commentary on catastrophe activity and Covid-19 impacts but does not present a single gross prior-year movement figure in narrative; the gross triangle was used as the authoritative source. The gross premium mix amounts available in the segmented analysis were for 2020 in the notes; a full 2021 statutory split by regulatory class was not clearly presented in the 2021 notes, so the provided mix reflects the latest available regulatory table (2020) - users should treat these as approximate and dated.
